title: Creator Sponsor Rate Floor Clinic
oneLiner: Creators prove the minimum sponsor rate they can accept before algorithm fear turns into underpriced deals.
theme: 자산 방어 / 역전 - creator pricing power under algorithm anxiety.
targetUser: Newsletter writers, YouTubers, niche creators, and solo media operators negotiating sponsor packages while audience growth feels unstable.
keyUX: Creator enters audience size, engagement, production time, deliverables, niche proof, and recent distribution effort; the app calculates a rate floor, builds sponsor options, and produces a confidence memo.
requiredUISections: Audience proof header with reach, engagement, retention, and niche fit
Deliverable cost board for newsletter, video, short, podcast, and bundle options
Sponsor package ladder with floor, fair, and premium tiers
Objection simulator for lowball offers and performance-risk pushback
Distribution grind log showing daily promotion and guest-pitch effort
Client-ready rate defense memo and invoice terms drawer
sourceSignals: S1 - Reddit r/NewTubers, YouTube is harder in 2026 for new creators: https://www.reddit.com/r/NewTubers/comments/1qze9ep/yes_youtube_is_much_harder_in_2026_for_new/
S2 - Reddit r/Newsletters, newsletter monetization in 2026 still requires daily distribution work: https://www.reddit.com/r/Newsletters/comments/1s9uoqx/are_newsletters_dead_in_2026/
stitchPrompt: Build a production-grade web app prototype called "Creator Sponsor Rate Floor Clinic" for newsletter writers, YouTubers, and niche creators deciding the minimum sponsor rate they can accept. The first screen must be a working sponsor-pricing clinic with an audience proof header, deliverable cost board, production time calculator, sponsor package ladder, objection simulator, distribution grind log, and client-ready rate defense memo. Use realistic sample data: 18,400 newsletter subscribers, 42% open rate, 8,200 average YouTube views, three sponsor deliverables, eight hours production time, a lowball $450 offer, and a premium bundle at $1,800. Design direction: use the operator-dense profile with compact negotiation panels, tabular money/time math, sharp confidence badges, and one decisive action accent for the recommended floor. Do not make a marketing landing page; the first screen must be the working app.
